description:
Moncler Re/Icons celebrates the enduring spirit of pioneering icons. Cher ponders her highest mountains climbed and takes in the view from the top. 

“My biggest mountain climbed? I'm still doing it. It's not easy to get on top, but it's a b*tch to stay on top. So, staying is my biggest triumph.”

Cher defied all odds to not only reach the pinnacle, but to stay there. Refusing to be defined by others, she has spent decades harnessing reinvention and embracing evolution, leaping across the boundaries of music, film and fashion to continuously shape global style and command pop culture’s attention. Bridging past and future, iconic heritage with modern edge, she embodies a spirit of timeless innovation and defiant authenticity. A powerful testament to those who dare to lead rather than follow, Cher’s pioneering spirit transcends age, limits and boundaries, uniting generations through a shared vision of bold, authentic self-expression.
title: Cher. Pioneering Genres & Generations

description:
Remo Ruffini - entrepreneur, CEO, creative director, dreamer.

Remo Ruffini’s dream is a lived one. Drawing constant inspiration from different generations, cultures and - always - the mountains, he fuels tomorrow’s aspirations with today's accomplishments.

“The most important thing when you have a dream is consistency. I never dream too high or too far. There needs to be a concreteness, the right combination of dreams and reality. Then, you can begin to build.”

More than twenty years at the helm of Moncler have taught Remo Ruffini that intuition is best paired with an open mind, and that dreams go further when anchored with consistency, determination, and reality.

Explore ‘An Invitation To Dream’ on moncler.com.
title: An Invitation To Dream | Remo Ruffini

description:
Jeremy O. Harris - playwright, performer, philanthropist, dreamer.

Growing up in the American South, Jeremy O. Harris dreamed of family security, writing and  becoming “the most famous actor of all time.” 

“The dream is always kind of the same: keep my family secure and tell great stories.”

His storytelling career has taken him from the blank page, to Broadway and the West End, via the big screen: a dream life, manifested - and constantly evolving.

Destined for the stage, the ballerina’s instinctive interpretations of canonical roles have carved her out as a modern icon.

Laila Gohar - artist, tastemaker, designer, dreamer. 

Laila Gohar’s work is an invitation to the senses: touch, smell, taste, imagine, play. Working with food as a medium to engage and inspire, her work runs the gamut from highest echelon museums to family feasts at home. 

“It allows this space to wonder, is this real? Can I touch it? Can I not? If I touch it am I breaking the rules? Does it feel kind of good anyway.”

From chairs made of bread, to fantasy sausage cakes, she sees life through a surrealist lens that espouses escapism - and the right to dream.

“There is absolutely everything to be dreamt and imagined.”

Dreamer of spaces, Sumayya Vally has dedicated her design practice to expressions of hybrid identity and territory, often with the power to reanalyze and reframe history. 

The youngest person to ever design the Serpentine Gallery’s Architecture Pavilion in 2021, Vally has gone on to win many accolades, and was artistic director of the inaugural Islamic Arts Biennale, putting forth an entirely new and decolonial definition of islamic art.

“Art is about trying to find the answer to something, but actually, it reveals more questions.”

Arsham’s ‘future relics’ reimagine familiar objects as tomorrow’s fictional artefacts, transcending reality, time and space to capture the world’s imagination.

description:
Zaya - model, climate activist, dreamer.

Born and raised in the Brazilian Amazon, Zaya dreams of a better future, connected to nature and her indigenous heritage.

A member of the Kamurape and Guarani Mbya ethnicities, she is dedicated to sharing her ancestral knowledge to create better environments, not just for the land, but also in global cities. She dreams of a world where indigenous voices are heard in every aspect of modern life.

“Right now, I’m living the dream I wished for ten years ago.”

description:

32 PHOTOGRAPHERS INTERPRET THE ICONIC MONCLER MAYA JACKET

An exhibition and magnificent volume which examine the strength and beauty of love from different and sometimes contrasting points of view, through the vision, technique and imagination of the greatest photographers in the world. An exhibition which hinges on a single object, the iconic Maya duvet jacket - that has always been the essential symbol of all the Moncler world - interpreted according to the the most diverse sensibilities and creative approaches.

ART FOR LOVE, a private, invitation only exhibition event, created to support amfAR, took place on September 11th in NYC, during fashion week, at The New York Public Library, Stephen A. Schwarzman Building, 5th Avenue and 42nd Street. A silent auction was held in the hall and a contemporary online site on Paddle8, and the proceeds was entirely donated to amfAR.

Remo Ruffini, President of Moncler, comments: “I am very proud to be alongside amfAR once again and to contribute through Moncler to raising funds for the project ‘Countdown to a Cure’, the aim of which is to find a cure for AIDS by 2020. The progress that has been obtained in the fields of research, prevention and education thanks to amfAR reinforces my enthusiasm for our involvement in this incredible cause”.

The exhibition takes the viewer on a journey that twists and turns through rugged adventure and delicate beauty, stopping for a touch of humour, sometimes veering into surreal or fantastically pop

description:
Versailles meets abstraction in the Moncler Gamme Rouge for the Spring-Summer 2016 season.
Giambattista Valli has once again decided to reinvent the tenets of a sporting discipline as it measures itself against fencing. In doing so it teams the sport’s precision with decorative details that recall aristocratic elements combining baroque and rococo.
It is a sporting pursuit that features allegorical allure, but here it is given a feminine interpretation with highly contemporary garments featuring Moncler’s outstanding signature technological research into materials.
Technical dentelle lace, embroidered PVC teamed with rebrodé mesh, a black and white checked print with a flocked effect on technical organza and tulle with applications that simulate floral ton-sur-ton rocaille stucco. The creative subplot is played out entirely in an overlapping patchwork effect: a sophisticated set of embroideries in which ivory white prevails, with red and black incursions. The principle underscoring the collection blends alternating geometrics with a soft effect. The volumes are clean-cut, with ample, well-defined cocoons which put the waistline, always an important and focal point, in the spotlight.
More on moncler.com
title: Moncler Gamme Rouge Spring-Summer 2016 Show

description:
Once upon a time, in a timeless time and a placeless place, in galaxies far away, there were two very young twins, with hair lighter than the midnight sun and eyes of a clear sky-blue. The two twins, Lucky and Pyper, lived alone and they loved each other very much. 

Thus it was one crystal-clear winter’s morning, without planning a direction or a destination, they set off to explore unknown terrain. For weeks and weeks, although in all truth nobody really knew how many days, moments or years it took them, they crossed heroic, deserted lands. They were together, and they were happy. That was all that mattered.

description:
THE MONDUCK STORY

The world's most famous down jacket celebrates its 60th anniversary. A comic celebrates its birthday.

One talks about the down jacket born in the mountains for reasons of necessity and adventure -- to be able to climb the Himalayas or cross Alaska -- then produced and re-invented on an unstoppable course, first in the mountains and then in the city. 
A creative and manufacturing history that has brought Moncler to a global presence, to dress everyone, at any temperature, without limitations on age or environment. 

Six decades of invention and innovation, the comic's panels lead us through the many facets of the brand's history. Decades in colour or in black and white, one different from the next in its perception, focusing on the key passages, the blend of technology and aesthetics that turned the down jacket into an iconic object: one with a transversal use, according to needs and times.

Already found within each garment, the duck (the brand's icon) now comes out to the forefront as the hero of the new global Moncler. A down jacket that is more than that, it is for everyone on every occasion.

Watch the third episode on http://moncler.com/the-monduck-story

Moncler Grenoble went back to the New York for the third year, taking center stage with a winter fairy tale at Wollman ice-skating rink, in the heart of Central Park.
180 professional athletes were synchronized skating, in monochrome teams of three, performin an impressive dance while presenting the new Autumn/Winter collection. Luam who has worked with celebrities such as Beyonce, Rihanna, Kelly Rowland and Britney Spears thoughtfully choreographed the act. An orchestra of New York based musicians provided the soundtrack.

Inspired by the Sixties, the collection showcases warm furs, soft wools and futuristic fabrics. The surprising mix of shapes are created with the use of plastic, suggesting a new and sophisticated identity. Women`s garments are snug and form a cocoon like silhouette around the figure. Coats and jackets are designed as protective shells in Naplak, a classic material used for bags in the sixties. Glossy, lively substantial, it-s an evolution of the celebrated Moncler Laque. Transparent PVC inserts allow a glimpse of the inner padding, which offers a subtle , futuristic effect to the classic puffer jacktets. The colour palette is neutral and conjures up a vision of mountains with hues of ice, stone and snow. Contrasting colours appear in navy blue and bright red.

A homage to the mountain and its conquerors was created in the form of the two sunglasses, LINO and ACHILLE, suitable for downhill runs and also as classic sunglasses for everyday use.

Made from the polyamide-based material MYLON, developed and patented by MYKITA, the frames are very light, extremely durable and individually adjustable to the wearer.

Both models are available in the colours red, blue and in a classic black. The frames are fitted with mineral glass lenses boasting excellent durability and clarity of vision, and reveal the MYKITA & Moncler logo when breathed on. The glasses come with a padded carry pouch for easy transport.
